540617b11b412f63.c: Each section is judged on what a normal person or community gets today, not on roadmaps. S means best in class, A excellent, B good, C mixed, D weak, and F missing or unusable. A tier can be empty. Inside a tier, apps are listed from best to worst.

Facts come from each app's own website, documentation, source code, app store listings and policies, plus reputable press and security research. Where we couldn't verify something, we didn't count it. Every comparison page lists its sources with dates.

Matrix and XMPP are ranked as networks with their best-known apps (Element and Movim). Kloak shut down in October 2026, so it is F everywhere; its page records what it offered. Things change quickly, so treat this as a snapshot.

03274eeefd44dae9: A cozy, open-source Matrix app with Discord-style voice rooms, shared calendars and photo albums. It is essentially one developer's project, still pre-1.0, with no macOS or iPhone app.
574b3649f0454628: Commet is a free, open-source app (a client) for Matrix, the open, federated chat network. You sign in with an account on any Matrix homeserver, and Commet shows your spaces and rooms in a Discord-like layout with voice rooms, calendar and photo album rooms, and several accounts logged in at once. It has been developed since 2023, mostly by one person, and is at version 0.5.0 (September 2026).

88668ea6b5fa8e5e: Much of what people say about Matrix is really about one server or one app. These are the three layers:
029bd6edb2340563: The protocol: Matrix itself is an open standard kept by the Matrix.org Foundation, a UK nonprofit. Anyone can build servers and apps for it.
f9660340a3c566c4: The homeserver: your account lives on a server you choose. matrix.org is the largest public one, and its rules (18+, verified email, 10 MB free uploads) don't apply on other servers or on your own.
a7213c4394170694: The app: Element is the main client, made by the company Element, which now focuses on governments and businesses. Element X is its newer mobile app and Element Classic the older one. Other clients, including the Discord-style Sable and Commet, work with the same account.
226627b865b86f63: Unless a cell says otherwise, this page describes Matrix as most people meet it: Element on the matrix.org homeserver.

aa5827f8d9d992c6: Sable is a free, open-source app (a client) for Matrix, the open, federated chat network. It doesn't run the network itself: you pick a Matrix homeserver such as matrix.org or sable.moe, and Sable gives you a Discord-like look with spaces, voice rooms, polls and themes on top. It started in February 2026 as a fork of the Cinny client and was rewritten from scratch as version 2.0 on 10 October 2026.

73ff5f5355903eff: On SerikaCord, DMs, group DMs and their calls are end-to-end encrypted by default for new conversations. In Movim, OMEMO encryption is optional, support differs between XMPP apps, and group calls aren't end-to-end encrypted. Our encryption is new (October 2026) and not audited, and it doesn't cover server channels either.
7bf1a176fcfc7a35: SerikaCord has named roles with per-channel permissions, onboarding questions, rules screening, AutoMod, an audit log, threads and forum channels. Movim's Spaces arrived in April 2026, need an ejabberd server, and use basic chatroom ranks.
cfa3682bebd47550: SerikaCord has apps for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android plus the web app. Movim is a web app only, which you can install from the browser. On iPhone, SerikaCord is also web-only for now.
7ffb299a4c3a5120: Many Discord bots work on SerikaCord after changing the API address, and our consent-based bridge mirrors a Discord server. On XMPP, bots have to be rewritten, and the Slidcord gateway connects only your own Discord account.
236ff92beb44130a: More than one person behind it
41f6177b9ee8fd8f: Movim is maintained mostly by one person alongside a day job, with about 2,300 EUR raised in 2026. SerikaCord is a small team too, so this edge is modest.
d50b47c46fce4d9c: XMPP is an IETF standard with thousands of independent servers. No company can shut it down or change the rules for everyone. SerikaCord is one central service run by one company.
3b472388d9e4adf0: Federation and your choice of app
b5ac3bef962c83a7: Federation means you can sign up on any server, or your own, and still talk to everyone else. The same account works in Movim, Conversations, Gajim, Dino and other apps. Self-hosted SerikaCord instances don't connect to serika.chat.
eb1caa370172bacd: Real open source you can host for anyone
e092a903f8bdc10a: Movim is AGPL-3.0, so you can run it for any group, including at work, as long as you share your changes. SerikaCord is source-available, not open source, and self-hosting is allowed only for personal, non-commercial use.
603a2c77bb385b2a: Slidge gateways connect XMPP to Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix accounts. SerikaCord only bridges to Discord.
e89315fa383084b7: Movim mixes chat with public blogs and Communities that can be read without signing in, and has full-text message search since November 2025. SerikaCord is focused on chat and has nothing like the blogs.
298bcec6772ba6db: No company and no data business
cad9656df61b405f: Movim is a donation-funded project, and mov.im is hosted in the EU. If you want chat run by a community rather than a company, it fits, though SerikaCord also has no ads and doesn't sell data.
